question: Under what condition may an animal be offered, and how many are to be given according to the stated teaching?
premises: If there is a particular desire, that animal may then be offered.
In that case one should give so many animals, thus.
This is as said by Maheshin.
inference: Offering of an animal is not obligatory, but if a particular desire arises, one offers it and gives so many animals as Maheshin has said.
uncertainties: The quantity tāvat is left indefinite in this verse.
The nature of viśeṣa kāṅkṣā is not specified here.
plain_english: But if there is a particular desire, one should then offer that animal; one should give so many animals, thus as said by Maheshin.
